title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government has released a response to the Committee's 2020 report on AI and public standards, outlining its commitment to strengthen regulatory oversight, transparency and accountability in the use of AI. The response details concrete measures such as establishing standards for data quality, testing and auditing, and setting up new governance frameworks for public sector AI deployments.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: This document explains the EU’s new 2024/1689 regulation that standardises rules for artificial intelligence across member states. It also details how the regulation updates or changes existing EU laws and directives related to AI.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual outlines its strategy for overseeing artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, aiming to safeguard exam integrity and student fairness by setting clear rules, monitoring AI tools, and providing guidance to exam boards and providers. The policy was released after a joint request from the Secretaries of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how copyrighted works are used to train and develop AI systems, highlighting legal risks, ethical concerns, and practical challenges. It offers recommendations and best‑practice guidance for policymakers, industry stakeholders, and creators to balance innovation with copyright protection.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has replied to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining its plan to strengthen AI regulation, boost research funding, and protect national interests. It will focus on ethical AI development, enhance oversight mechanisms, and keep the UK at the forefront of global AI innovation.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the scope, objectives, and responsibilities of a committee tasked with reviewing artificial intelligence and its impact on public standards. It also includes FAQs that clarify the review process and key considerations for stakeholders.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of Artificial Intelligence, presenting its views on how AI should be regulated and overseen. The submission outlines CSPL’s concerns and suggestions for improving AI accountability and policy frameworks.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy examines how artificial intelligence will reshape the rules governing medical products, ensuring they remain safe and effective. It also provides guidance on applying the AI White Paper principles to develop, test, and monitor AI-powered medical devices in compliance with regulatory standards.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: We aim to become the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential defence organisation in AI for our size. Our strategy focuses on developing advanced AI capabilities that enhance operational readiness and strategic advantage while upholding ethical and responsible practices.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report examines how copyright‑protected works are used to train AI systems and evaluates compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It identifies current practices, potential legal gaps, and recommends strategies to balance creators’ rights with AI innovation.
